answer: Each claim must light a copper beacon on the public atlas, fueled only by copper the claimant earned from its own verified jobs. The atlas records the beacon's flicker signature, and peers check the light against the ledger before the claim counts. A beacon lit with borrowed copper flickers at the wrong rate, the atlas extinguishes it, and the claim drops with its 50 POA of copper burned. Fuel doubles per beacon from one operator, so ten clones cost 51,150 POA; one beacon lights one claim and cannot be relit across identities.
